ζάγκλη.definition: = sq., Nic.Al.180; an ancient name of Sicilian Messene, from the shape of the natural mole which forms the harbour, Th.6.4, etc

Ζαγρεύς.definition: son of Zeus and Persephone, slain by the Titans and resuscitated as Dionysus, AlcmaeonisFr.3 , cf. E.Fr.472.11 , Call.Fr.171, Nonn.D.10.294; identified with by A.Fr.228

ζαής.definition: Ep. Adj. strong-blowing, stormy, Il.12.157, Od.5.368, prob. cj. in Hes.Th.253; Od.12.313 ; AP9.290

ζάθεος.definition: also E.Tr.256 , 1075 ; poet. Adj. :—very divine, sacred, of places favoured by the gods, Il.1.38, al. , h.Ap.223; Pi.P.5.70, I.1.32, cf. B.2.7; Id.5.10; Id.10.24; E.Ba.121 , etc.; A.Fr.284; of things, Hes.Th.253; Pi.P…

ζάκοτος.definition: exceeding wroth, Il.3.220, Theoc.25.83; of things, Pi.N.6.53; Id.Pae.9.18

ζάλη.definition: squall, storm, driving rain, A.Ag.656, S.Aj.352 , etc.; Pl.R.496d; by a storm of winds, Id.Ti.43c; Hp.Insomn.89; Plu.2.993e; of the fiery rain from Aetna, A.Pr.373: metaph., storms, distresses, Pi.O.12.12; Procop.Gaz.…

ζάπλουτος.definition: very rich, Hdt.1.32, E.Andr.1282, Lib.Decl.30.12, Jul.Ep.89b

ζατρεφής.definition: Ep. Adj. well-fed, fat, goodly, Il.7.223; Od.4.451

ζαφελής.definition: violent, with Adv. Id.; cf. Suid.:—also Nic.Al.556, EM408.17

ζάχρυσος.definition: rich in gold, E.Alc.498, IT1111 : in late Prose, Lib.Or.11.140

Ζβελσοῦρδος.definition: divinity worshipped in Thrace, Rev.Ét.Gr.26.247:—also in forms or etc

ζειρά.definition: a wide upper garment, girded about the loins and falling over the feet, worn by Arabians, Hdt.7.69; by Thracians, ib.75, X.An.7.4.4: Hsch.; but is prescribed by Gramm. in Reitzenstein Ind.Lect.Rost.1892/3 p.10

ζελᾶς.definition: gen. and dat. Thracian word, = Choerob.in Theod.1.145: but dat. Eup.ibid., cf. Hsch.s.v. Phot. s.v

ζέσις.definition: seething, effervescence, boiling, Pl.Ti.66b, Ocell.2.9, etc.; Gal.16.577; ib.661; up to boiling heat, Plu.2.690c: metaph., Pl.Cra.419e; Arist.de An.403a31

ζεστολουσία.definition: washing in hot water, Theon ap.Gal.6.208,212

ζευγάριον.definition: Dim.of a puny pair or team, esp. of oxen, Ar.Av.582; Id.Fr.109; ib.387, cf. PCair.Zen.251.7

ζευγίππης.definition: in pl., dub. l. in D.S.19.106

ζευγίσιον.definition: rating of the Arist.Ath.7.4, cf. Poll.8.130

ζευγίτης.definition: the third of Solon's four classes of Athenian citizens, so called from their being able to keep a team of oxen, Arist.Pol.1274a20, Ath.4.3, Lex ap.D.43.54, IG12.45.40, etc

ζεῦγμα.definition: that which is used for; bridge of boats, AP9.147 ; D.H.9.31, cf. Plu.2.174e, etc.; pier or platform formed by lashing several vessels together, Plb.3.46.2, Plu.Marc.14, 15

ζεῦγος.definition: yoke of beasts, pair or; carriage drawn by a yoke of beasts, a chariot, Hdt.1.31; ib.199; And.1.45; Hyp.Lyc.5; wagons, SIG124 ; Th.4.128; racing- car, = Id.5.50; A.Fr.346; Pl.Ap.36d ; a hired chariot, Id.Ant.6; with w…

ζευξίγαμος.definition: she that yokes in marriage, epith. of the planet Venus, Cat.Cod.Astr.1.173

ζευξίλεως.definition: subjugator of men, of a king, S.Fr.133

Ζεύς.definition: nom. Il.1.175, al., once written; of other deities, = Il.9.457; S.OC1606, SIG1024.25 ; of non-Greek divinities, Pi.P.4.16, etc.; freq. of Semitic Baalim, Z. etc., OGI620 ), etc.; Z. = Pers. Ahuramazda, ib.383.41

Ζέφυρος.definition: any westerly wind, Il.9.5: coupled with 21.334; opp. Od.5.332, 19.206; 5.295, 14.458; Arist.Pr.946a17; but ib.943b21; Il.11.305; of horses, 19.415; later, the due West wind, opp. Arist.Mete.363b12, cf.Mu.394b26; but r…

ζῆλος.definition: later Ep.Phil.3.6 codd. opt; c. gen. pers., zeal for one, S.OC943; in emulation of him, Plu.Thes.25; Luc.Dem.Enc.57: abs., passion, PGrenf.1.1.13

Ζηνοδότειος.definition: of the School of Zenodotus, D.L.2.15

Ζηνοδοτήρ.definition: giver of Zeus, i.e. of his counsel, AP9.525.7

Ζηνοποσειδῶν.definition: Zeus-Poseidon, a divinity worshipped in Caria, Macho ap. Ath.8.337c, cf. 2.42a, CIG 2700 add.; Dor. GDI5163b12

Ζηνόφρων.definition: gen. knowing the mind of Zeus, epith. of Apollo as revealing Zeus' will in oracles, AP9.525.7

Ζηνώνειος.definition: of Zeno, D.L.1.19; Z. Ph.2.460; Stoic philosopher, D.L.7.5:—also Dor. Cerc.9.16

ζῆτα.definition: indecl., the letter Pl.Cra.419b, etc.; of the sixth book of the Iliad, POxy.930.15 , Epigr.Gr.1095

ζιβύνη.definition: = LXXIs.2.4, Ph.Bel.92.44, Porph. ap. Eus.PE3.12: Hsch.:—Dim. Id

ζιγγίβερις.definition: Edict.Diocl.32.68 , ; or Dsc. and Gal. ll. cc.:-an Arabian spice-plant, the root of which was used in medicine, prob. ginger, Dsc.2.160, Gal.6.572, 11.880. through Skt. śṛṅgaveram and a Prakrit singaber.)

ζιζάνιον.definition: a weed that grows in wheat, = II, prob. darnel, Lolium temulentum, Gp.2.43, EM411.46: pl., Ev.Matt.13.25, Gp.10.87.1

ζόφος.definition: nether darkness; generally, gloom, darkness, Hes.Sc.227, Plb.18.20.7, Arist.Mu.400a8, Ep.Hebr.12.18, Plu.Alc.28, Luc.DMort.15.2; the gloom of winter, Pi.I.4.18: metaph., . . Plu.2.48c

ζυγάδιον.definition: a kind of shoe, prob. in Suid. s.v

ζύγαινα.definition: the hammer-headed shark, Epich.59, Arist.HA506b10, Philotim. ap. Gal.6.727, Ael.NA9.49, Opp.H.1.367

ζύγαστρον.definition: at Delphi, = SIG241.49,146 , Delph.3.205 , Phot; in pl., fastenings, Sch.Theoc.7.78

ζυγόν.definition: yoke of a plough or carriage, Il.5.799, 23.392; 5.731, cf. Od.3.383; Hes.Op.815, cf. 581; Il.24.576: prov., 'to be in the same boat', Aristaenet.2.7, Zen.3.43; Herod.6.12

ζῦθος.definition: beer of northern nations, Posidon.15J., Str.3.3.7, D.S.5.26. in the older Pap.: freq. accented in codd., but Phot., in verse, Poet. ap. D.Chr.32.82, Colum.10.116.)

ζῦτος.definition: = PCair.Zen.176.4 , al., PPetr.3p.327 , UPZ149.14 , PMag.Par.1.908, OGI200.16 :—also PHib.1.113.6 , Glauc. ap. POxy.1802.42

ζωάρκεια.definition: means of subsistence, Sch.E.Hec.362: Anon.Prog.inRh.1.599 W.: support life, Gramm. in Reitzenstein Ind.Lect.Rost. 1892/3 p.10

ζωαρκής.definition: life-supporting, Milet.6.18 , cf. Procl.H.1.2, Nonn.D.25.178; PLond.5.1729.17, al.; the necessaries of life, Phot

ζωγάνης.definition: slave-king at festival in Babylon, Beros.3

ζῳδαρίδιον.definition: Dim. of tiny figure, HeroSpir.2.34, Wiener Denkschr.47.59

ζῳδάριον.definition: = foreg., Dim. of animalcule, as a; = I, IG22.1491.4, Inscr.Délos 298 A31 , SIG2588.31 , HeroSpir.2.34, PMag. Leid.V.10.1

ζωηφόρος.definition: life-bringing, Them.Or.19.228d, Sch.Il.8.70; line of life, in palmistry, Cat.Cod.Astr.7.238

ζωμοτάριχος.definition: stewed salt-fish, as a nickname, Alex.42

ζωνῖτις.definition: in belts or seams, Dsc.5.74; cf. III.2

ζωόνυχον.definition: a name of the plant Ps.-Dsc.4.133

ζῳότης.definition: animal nature, Demetr.Lac.Herc.1055.15, Plu.2.1001b, A.D.Pron.6.24, Gal.19.163, Porph.Gaur.16.5; vitality, Dam.Pr.58

ζωπύρειος.definition: medicine named after the physician Zopyrus, Orib.Fr.125, cf. Gal.14.205, Paul.Aeg.7.11

Ζωστήριος.definition: of (a place on the west coast; = dub. in PLond.2.402.8 , cf.Gloss

ζῳύφιον.definition: Dim. of Ath.5.210c, Gal.6.666, Hsch., cj. for in S.E.P.1.41

ζάημι.definition: = part. Hsch.: 3sg. Id.: but Id. is connected with

ζαμενής.definition: poet. Adj. very strong, mighty, raging, h.Merc.307 ; Pi.P.9.38, N.4.13, cf. Sammelb. 5829.8: once in Trag., word of violence or enmity, S.Aj.137 ; also in late Ep., Opp.C.3.448: neut. as Adv., Nic.Th.181:—in form Orac…

ζατόω.definition: = EM408.11, cf. Hsch.:—Med. with aor. Pass., = Id. s.v

ζέννυμι.definition: = Philagr. ap. Orib.5.17.7, PHolm.15.22,al.: —Pass., Dsc.2.70, Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.104

ζεοποίιον.definition: mill for grinding prob. in AB261

ζευγηλασία.definition: the driving a yoke of oxen, Eust.361.13

ζευγηλατέω.definition: drive a yoke of oxen, X.An.6.1.9, Dialex.7.2

ζευγηλάτης.definition: the driver of a yoke of oxen, teamster, S.Fr.616, X.An.6.1.8, PFay.112.6 , Dialex.7.2: pl., D.S.31.24:—a fem. S.Fr.878

ζευγίζω.definition: yoke in pairs, unite, in Pass., PGrenf.1.1.1, LXX1 Ma.1.15,Aq.Nu.25.3

ζευγοτροφέω.definition: keep a yoke of beasts, Poll.8.132

ζευγοτρόφος.definition: keeping a yoke of beasts, IG22.1576.73 , Plu.Per.12

ζευγοφορέομαι.definition: Pass., to be drawn by a yoke of oxen, cj. in Ph. Bybl. ap. Eus.PE1.10

ζευκτήρ.definition: one who yokes or joins: hence Adj. the straps of the yoke, J.AJ12.4.6, cf. Hsch. s.v

ζευκτήριος.definition: fit for joining or yoking; as Subst., = yoke, Id.Ag.529, POxy.934.5 ; = II, Act.Ap.27.40

Ζεφυρίη.definition: = the west wind, Od.7.119. metri gr.]

ζεφυρίτης.definition: = foreg. I, epith. of the month of March, Lyd.Mens.4.152: fem. = foreg. I, Orph.H.81.1; = foreg. III, epith. of Aphrodite, as worshipped in Cyprus, Call.Epigr.6; cf. I

ζηλήμων.definition: gen. jealous, Od.5.118; and late Ep., as Call.Dian.30, Opp.C.3.191, Musae.36, 37; AP3.7

ζηλοτυπέω.definition: to be jealous of, c. acc; envy, Cic.Att.13.18.2 ; Jul.Or.5.167c

ζηλοτυπία.definition: jealousy, rivalry, envy, Aeschin.3.81, Com.Adesp.16.20D.; Plu.Per.10; Luc.Cal.2; Plu.2.276b; LXXNu.5.15: pl., Phld.Rh.2.139S

ζηλόω.definition: c. acc. pers., vie with, emulate, Th.2.37, Pl.R.553a, Michel 1007.29 :—Pass., Phld.Rh.1.125S., etc.: c.acc. rei, Th.2.64; in bad sense, to be jealous of, envy, Hes.Op.23, cf. h.Cer.168, 223, Theoc.6.27; LXXSi.9.1: abs…

ζημιόω.definition: fine, mulct in a sum of money, c. dat. rei, Hdt.6.21, cf. 136; Th.2.65; Pl.Lg.936a; also Lycurg.Fr.40 ; deprive of . . , Lyd.Mag.2.19:—Pass., to be fined or amerced in a thing, c. dat. rei, Antipho2.4.7; Pl.Lg.766d; i…

ζημιωτής.definition: one who punishes, Sch.rec.A.Pr.77; executioner, Eust.1833.53

ζητεύω.definition: poet. for sq., Hes.Op.400, h.Ap.215, h.Merc.392: Dor. Alcm.33.8

ζήτημα.definition: that which is sought, Hp.VM3; a thing not easy to find, of Pentheus’ mutilated limbs, E.Ba.1139; of God, Secund.Sent.3. II. inquiry, question, S.OT278, Act.Ap.15.2,al.; esp. of a philosophic nature, Pl.Lg.631a; ib.891…

ζητημάτιον.definition: Dim. of foreg. II, Arr.Epict.2.16.20, Lib.Decl.46 Pr.2

ζητητέος.definition: one must seek, Id.Nu.761, Sannyr.8; . . Pl.Phlb.58d

ζητητής.definition: seeker, inquirer, Pl.R.618c; at Athens, commissioners to inquire into extraordinary offences to to recover moneys owing to the State, And.1.14 , Lys.21.16, D.24.11, Pl.Com.125

ζήτρειον.definition: or a place of punishment for slaves at Chios, Eup.19D., Theopomp.Com.63, cf. EM411.33, Eust.837.44: prob. in Herod.5.32, cf. Choerob. ap. EM l.c.: metaph. in dat. pl. 'treadmills', dub. in Phld.Oec.p.44J.:—the forms A…

ζοφοδορπίδας.definition: supping in the dark or in secret, of Pittacus, Alc.37 B, cf. Plu.2.726a: in Theognost.Can.20, Zonar.; Hsch., Suid

ζοφομηνία.definition: = Hsch., Gramm. in Reitzenstein Ind.Lect.Rost. 1892/3 p.10

ζύγιον.definition: = III.1, Callix.1, cf. Aq., Sm. Pr.11.1

ζύγιος.definition: epith. of Hera as patroness of marriage, A.R.4.96, Musae.275; also of other divinities, as Aphrodite, IG3.171, cf.AP7.555 , Hsch

ζυγίτης.definition: the rower who sat on the mid- most of the three banks, like Sch.Ar.Ra.1106

ζυγόδεσμον.definition: yoke-band, i.e. a band for fastening the yoke to the pole, Il.24.270, cf. PFay.121.5 ; of the Gordian knot, Plu.Alex.18, etc.: pl., Procl.H.1.31, AP9.155 , 741, etc.:—also Artem.2.24, Them.Or.2.30b

ζυγοκέφαλον.definition: tax on land at so much a jugum, CIG2712.5 , Just.Nov.17.8

ζυγοκρούστης.definition: one who uses a false balance, Artem.4.57

ζυγομαχέω.definition: struggle with one's yoke-fellow; generally, struggle, quarrel, Com.Adesp.207, cf. Hyp.Fr.245, Procop.Gaz.p.141 B.; . . Phld.Herc.223.8; D.39.6; Men.673; Plu.Cat.Ma.21, cf. Chor. in Hermes 17.235; Gal.10.963

ζυγοποιέω.definition: make yokes, wrongly cited by Poll.7.115 fr. Ar.Pl.513

ζυγοστάσιον.definition: weigh-house, CIG3705 (Apollonia ad; zygostasii munus, office of Cod.Just.11.28.1

ζυγοστάτης.definition: Dor. public weigher, Cod.Just.10.73.2 , Artem.2.37: metaph., of Zeus, Cerc.4.33

ζυγωθρίζω.definition: weigh, examine, Ar.Nu.745, acc. to Sch.: but acc. to Poll.10.26 from , lock up

ζύμη.definition: leaven, Arist.GA755a18, LXXEx.12.15; beer-yeast, PTeb.375.27 , etc.: metaph., of corruption, falsehood, Ev. Matt.16.6, etc

ζυμίτης ἄρτος.definition: leavened bread, Cratin.99 , Hp.Vict.2.42, 3.75, X.An.7.3.21, LXXLe.7.3, Sor.1.94, Philostr.Im.2.26

ζύμωμα.definition: fermented mixture, Pl.Ti.74d; of a fungus, Nic.Al.521, cf. 525 cum Sch. ad loc

ζύμωσις.definition: fermentation, Pl.Ti.66b, Plu.2.659b, Gal.16.661; a swelling of the liver, Hp.Epid.4.8

ζωγονέω.definition: = of a living tree, POxy.1188.4 :— Pass., S.E.M.1.264

ζωγραφέω.definition: paint from life, paint, Pl.R.598b; adorn with paint, Ar.Ec.996; Alex.98.16, cf. Nicostr. ap. Stob.4.23.62

ζωγραφία.definition: art of painting, Democr.28a; painting, v.l. in Philostr.Ep.22 ; IGRom.1.1272

ζωγράφος.definition: one who paints from life or from nature, Hdt.2.46, Pl.Grg.448c, 453c, Lg.656e, etc.: metaph., Id.R.501c: generally, painter, Luc.Herod.4, Epigr.41. , SIG682.3 , Pap. in Abh.Berl.Akad.1904.6 , EM412.53: so SIG960.13 , …

ζωγρία.definition: Ion. taking alive, or = Hdt.6.28,37; SIG700.30 or Plb.1.9.8, 1.79.4; or Str.11.11.6, Plb.1.82.2; to lose him by his being captured, ib.15.2, Str.8.4.2; Plb.5.86.5

ζωγρίας.definition: one taken alive, Ctes.Fr.29.3,9, Zos.1.51; LXXDe.2.34; D.S.25.10; ibid.; Memn.56.3

ζῴδιον.definition: Dim. of II, small figure, painted or; Astron., sign of the Zodiac, Arist.Metaph.1073b20; Id.Mete.343a24, cf. Plb.9.15.7, Zeno Stoic.1.34, Hipparch.2.1.3, al., Gem.1.3, Autol.1.10, etc.:— also Arat.544, Man.1.309, al

ζώζω.definition: late spelling of UPZ81ii19, Sammelb.1060, etc

ζωμεύω.definition: boil into soup, Id.Fr.591, cf. Phryn.PSp.68 B.:—Pass., Hp.Int.35, Dsc.Eup.2.122

ζωμήρυσις.definition: soup-ladle, Antiph.249, Philem.Jun.1.6, Anaxipp.6.1, IG22.1416 , Ath.3.126d, AP6.101

ζωμίδιον.definition: Dim. of a little sauce, Ar.Nu.389

ζωνάριον.definition: Dim. of sq., Anon.in Rh.114.19, Hdn.Epim.41

ζώνιον.definition: Dim. of Ar.Lys.72, Arist.Mir.832b23, AP5.157 , Plu.2.154b

ζωογονέω.definition: propagate or engender living creatures, of; to be viviparous, Thphr.HP7.14.3; produce alive, Luc.Am.19; of Zeus, producing Pallas alive from his head, Id.DDeor.8, cf. D.S.1.23

ζωογονία.definition: production of animals, Pl.Epin.980c, Ph.1.14; of living things, Dam.Pr.284; breeding of worms, Thphr.CP5.9.3; generation, Sor.1.2

ζωογόνος.definition: producing animals, generative, Aret.SD2.5, Orph.H.38.3; name of Apollo, AP9.525.7; producing life, Procl.Inst.155; Jul.Or.5.175c, Dam.Pr.267; ib.282; Procl.H.1.10

ζωοποιέω.definition: make alive, LXX4 Ki.5.7, cf. Ev.Jo.5.21; bring to life, Luc.VH1.22, cf. Sch.E.Alc.122; endow with life, Dam.Pr.78, al., cf. Procl.Inst.25:—Pass., ib.209

ζῳοπώλης.definition: selling animals, esp. for sacrifice, Hsch

ζωοτοκέω.definition: to be viviparous, opp. Arist.Pol.1256b13; viviparous animals, Id.GA732b8: generally Ph.1.263:—Pass., to be born alive, Arist.PA693b23

ζωοτόκος.definition: opp. Id.HA489a34, al; life-giving, Nonn.D.26.191, al

ζωόω.definition: impregnate, Aret.SD2.5:—Pass; quicken, make alive, LXXPs.79.18; endow with life, Dam.Pr.80, Phlp.in GC200.6:—Pass., Hp.Alim.38, Gal.19.174,180, Phlp.in GC151.5, Id.in de An.64.7, al.; Plot.1.1.10, cf. 4.4.28; Id.6.7.12

ζωπυρέω.definition: kindle into flame, cause to blaze; metaph., A.Th.290 ; Id.Ag.1034 ; Arist.PA670a25, cf. Plu.2.940c; to provoke him, Ar.Lys.682 ; increase it, Plu.Lyc.9; in Magic, quicken, fill with power, PMag.Leid.V.10.7

ζωπύριον.definition: = prob. in Dsc.3.95 (from; bellows, Phot., Suid

ζωροπότης.definition: drinking neat wine, Hedyl. ap. Ath.11.497d; Man.4.300; . . AP5.225

ζωφυτέω.definition: thrive, flourish, of trees or plants, POxy.1188.3 , cf. PLond.2.214 ; BCH44.79

ζανεκέως.definition: or Adv., Aeol. for cj. in Corinn.9; cf. Hsch

ζυγάδην.definition: Adv., jointly, in pairs, Ph.1.237, al., Phot., Suid
